text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet unblocked 50,000 tonnes of wheat from state reserves at a price of $85 per tonne in a move to alleviate the country's acute bread shortage.

-- Interim interior minister Bogomil Bonev and chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev had discussed coordinated action for tracing culprits for the country's severe economic crisis, the interior ministry said. @

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet would urgently begin work on calculating the total Iraqi debt to the Balkan country, which ranges between $1.2 billion and $2 billion under preliminary estimates, interim trade minister Daniela Boneva said.
-- Prices of Bulgarian-made cigarettes are expected to rise 2.5 times under a proposal by the trade ministry to replace fixed prices with minimum prices.

-- Bulgaria's central bank was discussing a possible raising of minimum capital requirements for a domestic banking licence to five billion levs from 1.4 billion levs and to 10 billions levs for a full licence from 2.2 billion levs, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria may sell a larger stake than the planned 25 percent in the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company, depending on talks with potential investors, interim deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- A International Monetary Fund negotiating team arrived in Sofia to discuss preparations for introduction of a currency board system in Bulgaria to stabilise its collapsing economy.

-- Bulgaria's interim industry minister Alexander Bozhkov said that of the 1,158 industry firms in Bulgaria 401 posted losses for the first nine month in 1996. He said that during his term the ministry's priorities would be privatisation, closing state loss-makers and fight against corruption.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet decided to raise wages and social benefits by 60 percent from March 1, setting the minimum monthly wage at 17,600 levs, up from the current 11,100 levs. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
